reviews.title: Ignores paid requests and current audience
reviews.text:
Rockbot is frustrating to use. Paid song requests are often ignored, audience votes rarely seem to make a difference, and the app even blocks downvotes on songs that were not requested.

It also treats completely different songs with the same title as if they are the same track. For example, “Jump” by Van Halen and “Jump” by Kris Kross apparently count as the same song, so requesting one can prevent you from requesting the other.

The paid request system is especially restrictive. You can only request a specific song once every 24 hours, even when you are paying points to request it. Logging out also seems to remove paid requests, which makes paying for them feel even more pointless.

There is also no clear way to see how many points you actually have. I recently bought 50 points and used 6 points each on four songs, which should have left me with 26 points. Instead, when I tried to boost a fifth song, the app told me I was out of points. There is no visible balance or useful transaction history to explain where the rest went.

Now the newest problem is that Rockbot seems to randomly skip songs whenever it wants, including songs that people have paid to request. If someone is spending money or purchased points to hear a song, the app should not simply skip it without an explanation or refund.

reviews.title: Frustrating model
reviews.text:
Rockbot is a great idea… in theory.

In practice, whoever pays to add songs apparently becomes the DJ, music director, and dictator of the gym. Nothing like trying to work out while being held hostage by someone else’s playlist.

I’ve been listening to Gloria Estefan and Phil Collins at the gym because apparently someone decided we’re all attending an ’80s nostalgia convention. Nothing against Gloria or Phil, but I didn’t sign up for that.

At least let non-paying users pick more than TWO songs. And maybe teach the app to learn the preferences of the people actually using it instead of constantly pushing its own playlist.

The concept is good. The execution is terrible.

I’m giving Rockbot one last chance before uninstalling. If I hear “Easy Lover” one more time, we’re done.

reviews.title: Broken app/scam
reviews.text:
The amount of times I have tried requesting songs at the establishment that uses this app, and the venue algorithm constantly skips my upvoted songs that me and others have upvoted and the app plays the venues algorithmic downvoted songs over the requested ones THAT ARE PAID FOR even though that is not how the app is supposed to work. I am tired of it and this is a broken app. They haven’t fixed it in years and at this point, they’re just scamming me.

Per their support and website if a song is up voted, it is supposed to play sooner and vice versa. If a song is downloaded, it is supposed to take longer to play yet it constantly does not play the songs that I up voted paid for other people up voted and the other songs are downloaded it’s broken and I’m tired of not saying anything about it for years

I’m literally paying for nothing at this point and it’s not right

reviews.title: Now it’s EVEN WORSE
reviews.text: (UPDATE) When I said do better, I didn’t mean do better by making it worse. First it was your requested songs being knocked down all the way to the bottom of the queue and forcing those terrible bland NPC techno music to play before yours, now it just goes offline when you try to request a certain song just for that song to get removed and you can’t request that song anymore because of the venue being temporarily offline over and over again. I can go on forever but this review is already long enough. It’s very funny and sad at the same time to see an app go from a very fantastic unlimited requesting app to a very limited, more strict buggy and broken to the point where it’s just unusable. Just very sad.
